title: Unbounded native recursion in term comparison and hashing — adopt the GC's explicit worklist shape
purpose: Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M8 (MEDIUM, resource exhaustion), reviewed at `fd71c5e`: "Unbounded native recursion in term comparison and hashing. `term/compare/mod.rs:432` — deeply nested terms overflow the native stack (GC itself uses an explicit work queue and is safe; compare/hash do not)." RE-PINNED AT `a0359a2` (current main): NO DRIFT — `crates/beamr/src/term/compare/mod.rs:432` is still the recursive `cmp(left_element, right_element, atom_table)` call inside `compare_tuple_elements`. The finding is broader than the one cited line: there are THREE parallel comparison entry points, each recursing through the same shapes, plus the hasher. Comparison recursion sites at the pin: `compare_tuple_elements` (`compare/mod.rs:429-439`, recursive `cmp` at :432), `compare_tuple_elements_raw` (:441-451, `raw_cmp` at :444), `compare_tuple_elements_exact` (:453-463, `compare_exact` at :456); the list arms pass a recursive element comparator into `compare_lists_with` (:465-475 building the closures, applied at :485 and :493 — the list SPINE is already iterative, the ELEMENTS are not); the map arms (:498-508 -> `compare_maps_with` :510-526) recurse per key and per value via `sorted_map_entries` (:534-546, `sort_by` at :544) and `compare_map_entries` (:548-563); the closure arms recurse over free variables (`compare_closures_with` :620-629, `compare_closures_with_raw` :671-680). Hashing has the identical shape in `crates/beamr/src/term/hash.rs`: `hash_term` (:124-164) is re-entered by `hash_tuple` (:176), `hash_closure` (:211), `hash_map` (:222-223) and `hash_list` (:249 — again an iterative spine with a recursive head), and `hash_map` additionally sorts with `compare::exact_cmp` (:219). THE IN-REPO PATTERN THIS BRIEF ADOPTS: the GC does exactly this traversal without native recursion — `crates/beamr/src/gc/minor.rs:22` allocates `let mut work_queue = VecDeque::new();`, seeds it from the root set (:24-28), and drains it in a flat loop (:30-34) calling `rewrite_copied_object`; `crates/beamr/src/gc/major.rs:22-43` is the twin; the shared driver `crates/beamr/src/gc/mod.rs:213-260` (`rewrite_copied_object`, `work_queue` parameter at :217) pushes every child field back onto the caller's queue instead of descending. The GC therefore survives arbitrarily deep terms; compare and hash do not. REACHABILITY: `compare` is not an internal detail — `impl PartialEq for Term` (`crates/beamr/src/term/mod.rs:65-69`) calls `compare::partial_eq` -> `exact_eq`, and `impl Ord for Term` (`term/mod.rs:79-83`) calls `compare::raw_cmp`, so EVERY `==`/`<` on a `Term` anywhere in the tree (ETS `ordered_set` BTreeMap key comparisons, `constant_pool`, `interpreter/pattern.rs`, `ets/match_spec.rs`, the lists/maps stdlib BIFs, `jit/runtime_map.rs`, `etf/decode.rs`) is a potential overflow site, and `EtsKey`'s `Hash` impl (`term/hash.rs:43-47`) routes every ETS hash-table insert/lookup through `term_hash`. Ordinary Gleam/Erlang code builds the triggering shape without trying: nested tuples, nested lists-of-lists, or a list whose elements are themselves deep. Native stack overflow in Rust is not a catchable condition — it is a SIGSEGV/abort that takes the whole node down, so this is a remote-input-reachable availability defect wherever untrusted term shapes reach a comparison.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (RULED — work queue, not a depth budget). The review offers two shapes: rewrite compare/hash with an explicit worklist the way the GC already does, or impose a depth budget that raises a catchable error. THE RULING IS THE WORK QUEUE, on two independent grounds, and the tradeoff is stated here so the tear does not have to re-derive it.

(1) SEMANTIC FIDELITY. BEAM compares arbitrarily deep terms successfully; there is no `system_limit` on comparison depth in OTP. A depth cap makes a LEGAL Erlang comparison fail, which is a visible semantic change to `=:=`, `==`, `<`, term sort order, ETS key identity and map key identity. That would need its own justification, an OTP-divergence note in `docs/terminology.md`, and a number nobody can defend; the work queue needs none of that.

(2) THE SIGNATURES FORBID IT ANYWAY. A catchable error requires a `Result` return. The comparison surface is reached through `impl PartialEq for Term` (`term/mod.rs:65-69`) and `impl Ord for Term` (`term/mod.rs:79-83`), and the hash surface through `impl Hash for EtsKey` (`term/hash.rs:43-47`). Those are std trait methods with infallible signatures: `fn eq(&self,&Self) -> bool`, `fn cmp(&self,&Self) -> Ordering`, `fn hash<H>(&self,&mut H)`. A depth budget inside them could only express refusal by PANICKING (banned outside `cfg(test)` by the house bar) or by SILENTLY RETURNING A WRONG ANSWER (a correctness defect strictly worse than the crash it replaces). There is no third option short of removing beamr's `Term: Ord`/`Term: PartialEq` impls, which would ripple into every `BTreeMap`/`DashMap`/`assert_eq!` in the tree. The depth cap is therefore not merely less faithful; it is not implementable at the surface where the recursion actually lives.

D1 SHAPE — EXPLICIT LIFO STACK, NOT THE GC'S FIFO QUEUE. The GC is the precedent for "traverse with an explicit worklist instead of native frames", but its `VecDeque` is a FIFO because reachability does not care about order. Comparison DOES care: the result is the FIRST structural difference in left-to-right order, so the worklist must be a LIFO stack of pending `(left, right)` pairs with children pushed in REVERSE index order, and hashing must feed the hasher in the exact same pre-order it does today. State this difference explicitly in the module doc so the next reader does not "fix" it back to a queue.

D2 ALLOCATION POSTURE. Today compare is allocation-free except for `sorted_map_entries`. The rewrite keeps a `current` pair in a local and uses `Vec::new()` for the pending stack, which allocates nothing until the first push — so scalar, atom, pid, binary and flat-list comparisons stay allocation-free, and only genuinely nested shapes allocate. This is a judgment call recorded for the tear: no new dependency (no smallvec), no inline-array micro-optimisation in v1, no configuration.

D3 THE MAP-KEY RESIDUAL (named, not hidden). Map comparison must order entries by key term order, so `sorted_map_entries` calls `sort_by` with a comparator that is itself the term comparator (`compare/mod.rs:544`; the hash twin is `hash.rs:219`). After the rewrite that comparator is the ITERATIVE entry point, so a map appearing as a VALUE costs zero native frames. A map nested inside a map KEY still costs a constant number of native frames per nesting level, because each level's sort re-enters the comparator. That residual is bounded by map-in-map-key nesting depth (a shape ordinary code essentially never builds), is a factor-of-thousands improvement over the current per-element recursion, and MUST be documented in the module doc with the reason. If the builder finds a clean way to flatten it (e.g. precomputing per-map sorted key orders on the pending stack), that is welcome but is NOT required by this brief; what IS required is that the residual is named in code and in the handoff rather than silently inherited.

D4 ADJACENT SITE, EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE. `crates/beamr/src/mailbox/mod.rs:341-360` (`copy_term`/`copy_cons`) has the SAME defect and is arguably worse — `copy_cons` recurses on the TAIL (:354), so a flat list of N elements costs N native frames on every cross-process send. The review's M8 does not cover it and this brief does not fix it. Record it in the handoff as a board candidate (suggested id BEAMR-COPY-TERM-RECURSION) with the line citation; do not widen this lane.

D5 RED-FIRST OBSERVATION TECHNIQUE. A Rust stack overflow aborts the PROCESS, including from a spawned thread, so a naive `#[test]` cannot observe it cleanly. The probe therefore runs the deep comparison in a CHILD PROCESS and the parent asserts on the child's exit status: the failure is a clean parent-side assertion, not a torn test binary. Inside the child the work runs on a thread with a deliberately SMALL stack (`std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(...)`), which (a) makes the pre-fix overflow fast and deterministic instead of depending on the host's default stack, and (b) makes the post-fix green a STRONGER claim: the fixed code is safe against a small stack, which is the situation the wasm32 target actually runs in.

requirements.title: RED probe: deep-term compare and hash overflow the native stack, observed from a parent process
requirements.spec: Per D5: a new integration test `crates/beamr/tests/deep_term_recursion.rs`. A helper builds a deterministic deeply nested term WITHOUT recursion (an iterative loop writing N nested 1-tuples via `crate::term::boxed::write_tuple` into one large backing buffer, and the twin list shape `[[[...]]]` via `write_cons`); depth is a named `const` in the test, chosen so the pre-fix code overflows a small stack with margin and the post-fix code completes well inside it. The child leg is a `#[ignore]`d test function that runs the work on `std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(SMALL_STACK)` and exits 0 on success; the parent leg spawns `std::env::current_exe()` with `--ignored --exact <child test name>` and asserts `status.success()`, printing the child's status on failure. Four child legs: exact compare (`Term: PartialEq` via `==`), ordering (`Term: Ord` via `cmp`), table-aware `compare::cmp` with a real `AtomTable`, and `term::hash::term_hash`.
acceptance: Pre-fix the parent assertion FAILS with a non-success child status (SIGSEGV/SIGABRT from the child's stack overflow) on every one of the four legs — recorded as the fail-first evidence; post-fix all four legs exit 0

The parent test process is never itself aborted: the overflow is contained in the child, so `cargo test` reports a normal assertion failure and the rest of the binary still runs (this is the bounded-observation requirement — the child is the subject, the parent is the observer)
The term builders are iterative: no helper in the test file calls itself, so a pre-fix failure can only come from the code under test
Ten consecutive isolated runs of the file are stable in both directions (pre-fix red x10, post-fix green x10) — the depth constant carries enough margin that host stack differences cannot flip it

requirements.title: Comparison: explicit LIFO worklist across all three entry points
requirements.spec: Per D1/D2/D3: rewrite `crates/beamr/src/term/compare/mod.rs` so `cmp` (:58), `raw_cmp` (:72) and `compare_exact` (:198) each drive a flat loop over an explicit `Vec<(Term, Term)>` pending stack instead of re-entering themselves. Tuple arms (`compare_tuple_elements` :429, `_raw` :441, `_exact` :453) push remaining element pairs in reverse index order instead of recursing; list arms keep the existing iterative spine (`compare_lists_with` :477-496) but push head pairs onto the shared stack instead of invoking a recursive comparator closure; closure arms (`compare_closures_with` :620-629, `compare_closures_with_raw` :671-680) push free-variable pairs the same way; map arms (`compare_maps_with` :510-526, `compare_map_entries` :548-563) push key pairs and value pairs. `TermRank`/`ExactKind` classification, the BEAM rank order, atom-name comparison through the table (`compare_atoms_by_name` :183-196), number/bigint/binary/reference/pid comparison and every returned `Ordering` are UNCHANGED — this is a control-flow rewrite, not a semantics change. The module doc gains the D1 note (LIFO with reverse pushes, and why it is not the GC's FIFO) citing `gc/minor.rs:22-34` and `gc/mod.rs:213-260`, plus the D3 residual note.
acceptance: No function in `term/compare/mod.rs` re-enters `cmp`, `raw_cmp`, `compare_exact` or `exact_eq` other than through the `sort_by` comparator in `sorted_map_entries` (the D3 residual), and that one call site carries the documenting comment
The existing `term/compare/tests.rs` suite passes unmodified — no test is relaxed, retargeted or deleted to accommodate the rewrite

Allocation posture: the pending stack is created with `Vec::new()` and is never pushed for scalar, atom, pid, reference, binary, nil or flat-list-of-scalars comparisons; this is asserted by code shape and stated in the module doc, not by a new dependency

ZERO new `#[allow]`, zero `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`, zero `_ =>` catch-all arms introduced in the rank/kind matches (they stay exhaustive so a future term kind fails to compile until it declares its traversal)

requirements.title: Hashing: explicit worklist with a byte-identical digest stream
requirements.spec: Per D1: rewrite `crates/beamr/src/term/hash.rs` so `hash_term` (:124) drives a flat loop over an explicit `Vec<Term>` pending stack. `hash_tuple` (:170-178), `hash_closure` (:195-214), `hash_map` (:216-225) and `hash_list` (:243-259) push their children in reverse order instead of re-entering `hash_term`, so the byte sequence fed to `StableHasher` is UNCHANGED. `HashKind` discriminants, the FNV-style mixing (`StableHasher` :57-105), the bigint small-value canonicalisation (`hash_bigint` :180-193) and the map entry sort by `compare::exact_cmp` (:219) are all preserved verbatim.
acceptance: Digest stability wall: a new `#[test]` pins `term_hash` output for a fixed vector set (small int, atom, nil, float, bigint (both small-canonical and multi-limb), binary, tuple, proper list, improper list, map, closure-free-var-bearing term) to the values produced by the CURRENT code — captured from `main` at `a0359a2` BEFORE the rewrite and hard-coded, so any change to the fed byte stream fails loudly rather than silently repartitioning every ETS hash table
All existing `term/hash.rs` tests (:261-422) pass unmodified, including `equal_maps_hash_equal_regardless_of_entry_order` and `improper_list_tail_contributes_to_hash`
`hash_term` is not re-entered by any helper in the file except through the `sort_by(compare::exact_cmp)` comparator at :219 (the D3 residual, sharing compare's documented note)

requirements.title: Equivalence wall: the iterative comparator is observationally identical to the recursive one
requirements.spec: A proptest-backed differential wall (proptest is already a dev-dependency of `beamr`). Preserve the CURRENT recursive implementations as `#[cfg(test)]` reference oracles (`reference_cmp`, `reference_raw_cmp`, `reference_compare_exact`, `reference_hash_term`) inside the test modules of `term/compare/tests.rs` and `term/hash.rs`, and assert that for randomly generated term graphs of BOUNDED depth (shallow enough that the oracle cannot overflow — depth <= 16, arbitrary breadth) the iterative implementation returns the identical `Ordering`/`bool`/`u64` for every pair. Generation must cover every rank/kind including maps, closures with free variables, improper lists, bigints, floats (including NaN and -0.0 through `total_cmp`), and mixed int/float pairs for the `numeric_eq` arm.
acceptance: The differential property passes over at least 1,024 generated cases per arm with a fixed seed recorded in the test, and is deterministic across runs
The oracles are byte-copies of the pre-rewrite functions with only renaming applied, and a comment says so — a hand-rewritten oracle proves nothing
Fail-first recorded: deliberately perturbing one push order in the iterative tuple arm (e.g. forward instead of reverse) makes this wall go red, then restore
The oracles are `#[cfg(test)]` only and contribute zero bytes to the shipped library

boundaries: NO DEPTH CAP, NO NEW ERROR VARIANT, NO SIGNATURE CHANGE. `cmp`/`raw_cmp`/`exact_eq`/`numeric_eq`/`term_hash` keep their exact current signatures and return types; `impl PartialEq for Term`, `impl Ord for Term` and `impl Hash for EtsKey` are untouched. Anything that makes a legal Erlang comparison fail, or that widens these to `Result`, is a STOP — see the D-stance ruling.

SEMANTICS FROZEN: BEAM term order, `=:=` vs `==` coercion, map-entry sorting, float `total_cmp` handling, bigint canonicalisation and the hash digest byte stream are all byte-preserved. This is a control-flow rewrite. Any observable result change is a STOP.

MAP-KEY RESIDUAL IS NAMED, NOT SILENT: the constant-frames-per-map-key-nesting-level residual (D3) must be documented at the `sort_by` call sites in both files. Shipping the rewrite while pretending the residual does not exist is a tear condition.
OUT OF SCOPE, RECORD DO NOT FIX: `mailbox/mod.rs:341-360` `copy_term`/`copy_cons` tail recursion (D4); the other M-cluster findings; anything in `term/boxed`.

`crates/beamr/src/term/**` compiles on BOTH the threaded native closure and the cooperative wasm32 closure (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p beamr --no-default-features --features cooperative,json --locked`) — wasm32 has a ~1 MiB default stack, so this fix matters MORE there. Both wasm32 check legs stay green and the beamr-wasm 80-test count is untouched (no wasm-side test added by this brief).

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no new `_ =>` catch-all arms; no new dependencies (no smallvec/arrayvec); `crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` untouchable; no new config knobs (no tunable depth, no tunable stack reserve); NO-POLLING is not engaged by this brief (no threads, timers or wake paths are added or changed).

House LOC bar applies: `term/compare/mod.rs` is 688 lines at the pin and already over the 500-line advisory. The rewrite must not grow it further; splitting the exact/raw/table-aware drivers into a sibling module under `term/compare/` is the preferred shape if it grows.
verification: Full release battery at the final head: the committed 5-leg `gates.json` run (`fmt`; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` as a FRESH lint with `cargo clean -p beamr` and the Compiling line captured; `wasm32-check`; `wasm-tests` with the exact 80-passed carrier; `tests` workspace-wide), plus the cooperative wasm closure leg (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p beamr --no-default-features --features cooperative,json --locked`) and a prohibition grep sweep (`#[allow]`, `unwrap(`, `expect(`, `panic!` outside cfg(test), `_ =>` added in the touched files, run through `git -c diff.external= diff --no-ext-diff` per the DIFF-GREP TRAP). Isolation: the new `deep_term_recursion` integration binary 10x. FAIL-FIRST, both directions: (a) revert R2's tuple arm to the recursive `cmp` call -> R1's compare legs go red at the child exit status -> restore; (b) perturb one push order in the iterative tuple arm -> R4's differential wall goes red -> restore; (c) alter one byte fed to the hasher -> R3's digest wall goes red -> restore. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base (this brief is pinned at `a0359a2`): re-read `term/compare/mod.rs` recursion sites :429-463 / :477-496 / :510-563 / :620-680, `term/hash.rs` :124-259, `term/mod.rs:65-83` trait impls, and the GC worklist citations `gc/minor.rs:22-34` / `gc/major.rs:22-43` / `gc/mod.rs:213-260`; report any drift before building. Handoff carries: the chosen depth and stack-size constants with the margin argument, the pinned digest vector, the D3 residual text as landed, and the BEAMR-COPY-TERM-RECURSION board candidate.
